attempts.title: baseline: reference get_scan.c unchanged (scan-pid list + sampled LFU)
baseline: reference get_scan.c unchanged (scan-pid list + sampled LFU)
baseline: reference get_scan.c unchanged (scan_pids list + sampled LFU) to calibrate my host

scan-aware S3-FIFO v1 (structural 1/3): scan_pids folios -> scan_list evicted first (promote to main if a non-scan thread touched it), others S3-FIFO small(10%)/main CLOCK freq<=3 + ghost; scan-thread accesses don't bump freq
scan-aware S3-FIFO v1 retry (fix compile: name clash need_more, ctx param shadows BPF_PROG ctx)
lean scan-first LRU: scan_pids list evicted first (keep youngest 256), general list LRU via list_move on non-scan access, no hash metadata, skip LevelDB last page
scan-first FIFO hybrid: only scan-pid-inserted folios tracked (FIFO, skip file last page), rest left to kernel default reclaim; no metadata map, no accessed hook

scan-quarantine LRU v1 (structural 1/3): scan_pids folios -> FIFO scan_list evicted first above 256-page reserve; main_list true LRU (move-to-tail on non-scan access); GET hit on scan folio promotes to main
calibration: noop (kernel default reclaim) on my host pc318, to anchor same-machine comparison (everyone's cache_ext policies so far < 640)
calibration: unmodified noop (kernel default reclaim) on my host pc257, to measure baseline + diagnostic probes
ablation: reference get_scan with ONLY scan-list threshold 5000->256 (and no early return when scan_pages==0). Isolates threshold vs sampled-LFU/hash cost. Prior: lean LRU 632, ref 516.
floor test: empty struct_ops hooks ATTACHED via real loader (vs noop which never attaches). Measures cost of cache_ext attach itself; noop=642, scan-FIFO=600 on pc257
SLRU v1 (structural 1/3, focus-captain-nemo-slru-main): scan_list FIFO (reserve 256) + probation LRU + protected LRU (cap 3/4 cache, promote on 2nd non-scan access); evict scan>prob>prot

scan-first + sampled LFU (16 samples) with persistent freq history (LRU hash 200k keyed inode+index restores count on re-add); scan_list evicted first above 256 pages, GET-touched scan folios moved to gen. Lane: frequency for zipfian GETs (S3-FIFO 10% probation 585 was too short)

v3: scan-first LRU + probation list. New non-scan folios go to prob_list; first non-scan access promotes to main LRU. Evict order scan(>256) > prob > main. Hypothesis: readahead neighbours (~14KB/IO => ~3 junk pages per GET miss) were polluting LRU MRU end. Also: ablation 4ee45189 showed get_scan threshold fix only 516->547, so sampled-LFU itself loses to LRU (632).
SLRU v1 retry (structural 1/3; fix: cache_pages rodata u64->size_t): scan_list FIFO reserve 256 + probation LRU + protected LRU cap 3/4 cache; evict scan>prob>prot
v3 + SCAN_KEEP 256->2048 (8MiB reserve for unconsumed scan readahead). Tests whether scan-thread speed binds throughput (team sees rbytes positively correlated with throughput). Prior v3=649.
replication: jack-sparrow v3 (b65fa44f) unchanged on my host pc318 — same-host baseline for my composites; checks whether 649 > noop 642 holds across hosts

structural 1/3 2Q+ghost: scan list first (keep 256), prob list (A1in, promote on 2nd non-scan access), main LRU, LRU-hash ghost of prob evictions readmits to main; prob evicted while >1/4. Hypothesis: device is IOPS-saturated (rios ~11-12k in every run), so only demand-miss rate matters; kernel LRU-2 lacks freq filter for one-hit data blocks

ablation (reviewer): jack v3 + per-folio HASH metadata maintained in added/accessed/evicted/evict-cb but never affecting decisions. Same-host v3 baseline=618.65 (264e80e8). Tests whether hash-map overhead (not hit ratio) explains why my S3-FIFO(585)/LFU(572) and get_scan(~510) lose

structural 1/3 MQ-lite: scan list first, then probation (freq0 readahead junk), then 4 freq levels (1,2-3,4-15,16+) LRU-within-level, ghost LRU_HASH restores freq on re-read. Rationale: rios ~constant (~290/s, disk-IOPS-bound) across ALL team attempts so tput = ops/IO = GET hit ratio; page cache is 2nd-level behind LevelDB block cache, stationary Zipf => frequency wins. Prior best v3=649 (SCAN_KEEP 2048 = 636, reverted).

ablation of c53d4286: identical 2Q+ghost but scan-thread pages NOT special-cased (no scan list, scan accesses count). Tests hypothesis that scan pages are reused (Zipf scan starts / GET overlap) and scan-first eviction is what makes every team policy lose to noop (ops/IO: noop 2.23 vs scan-first 2.12-2.16)
calibration: unmodified noop on MY host pc258 (comment-only change). My v3=649 here; ahab noop on pc257=642. Needed to know whether v3 beats kernel default on this machine.

perf-eng: jack v3 + per-CPU array caches in front of scan_pids(tid) and inode_watchlist(ino) hash lookups (revalidate every 256 uses). Motivation: my ablation 9049727e showed +3 hash ops/event costs -3% (600 vs 618.65 same host), so per-hook CPU matters. Same-host v3 baseline 618.65

inversion test on bd194ffb (631): scan-thread-inserted folios admitted straight to main LRU instead of probation; GET-inserted still via prob/2nd-access. If scan pages are reused (scan-first eviction cost 593 vs 631), treating scan as hotness signal may help

structural 1/3 2Q-CLOCK (on bd194ffb, no scan special-casing): main list becomes freq CLOCK (access freq++ cap 7, no list_move; eviction halves freq>0 + rotates, evicts freq==0, up to 3 passes). Tests whether frequency retention beats LRU for Zipf GETs once scan-first is removed

v5 = v3 decisions (scan>prob>LRU main) but folio_accessed uses a direct-mapped ARRAY (slot=(ptr>>6)&(2^20-1), value=ptr|state, exact tag check) instead of watchlist+scan_pids HASH lookups; scan_pids only checked for scan-state folios. Tests CPU-overhead lever: davy-jones 9049727e showed decision-neutral HASH metadata costs ~3% (618->600). My noop on pc258=634, v3=649. Minor decision change: scan-thread access to a main/prob folio now refreshes it.

replication run 2 of my LFU+history (f32e85c6, 571.8): ahab showed identical code varies 593->631, so checking whether frequency lane really loses to LRU (same-host v3 runs: 618.7, 600.0*, 599.9*; *=v3 variants)

v5 retry (fix verifier: no ptr arithmetic): v3 decisions, folio_accessed uses direct-mapped ARRAY keyed by hash(ino,index) with exact (ino<<32^index) tag instead of watchlist+scan_pids HASH lookups. Tests CPU-overhead lever (davy-jones 9049727e: decision-neutral HASH costs ~3%). pc258: noop=634, v3=649.

structural 2/3 frequency-history (TinyLFU-2Q) on 18525923 (641): 4x64K count-min sketch of page (host,index) accesses w/ lazy epoch aging, survives eviction; insert -> main if sketch>=2 or ghost hit; main eviction = sampled LFU (16) on sketch estimate. Idea: Zipf favours long-term LFU; residency-only counts (get_scan) reset on refault

structural 2/3 TinyLFU-2Q (retry, fix clang-14 XADD-return compile error in aging counter): count-min sketch page history survives eviction; insert->main if sketch>=2 or ghost; main = sampled LFU(16) on sketch
replication 2 of v3 (b65fa44f, scored 649; comment-only change). ahab showed identical code varies 593->631, so noise ~+-5%; need repeat before trusting v3>noop(634) on pc258.

structural 2/3 TinyLFU-2Q (retry 2: hash on scalar host->i_ino, verifier rejected pointer math in sample cb): sketch page history survives eviction; insert->main if sketch>=2 or ghost; main = sampled LFU(16) on sketch

structural 1/3 (perf-eng lane): scan-first CLOCK with HASH-FREE per-folio ref bits in an ARRAY bitmap indexed by folio>>6 (struct-page index, 2^24 slots); folio_accessed = one array load/store, no relevance/scan-pid hash lookups, no list_move lock. v3 layout (scan>256 / prob->gen promote if ref / gen CLOCK). Same-host v3 family: 618.7/600.0/599.9; LFU+hist 571.8/587.1 (frequency lane abandoned)

structural 1/3 on cheap-metadata SLRU+ghost (v6): 4 lists scan>prob>main>hot; main=accessed once (the read), hot=2nd access, hot evicted first only if >3/4 of tracked pages; ghost ARRAY readmits evicted-hot folios straight to hot. All state in direct-mapped ARRAYs (no HASH). Motivation: team frequency policies (SLRU 592, 2Q+ghost 593/631, LFU 572-587) were all confounded by HASH cost (~3%, davy 9049727e); v5 showed ARRAY state ~free (634 vs v3 mean 638 = 649,627). pc258 noop=634.

structural 3/3 TinyLFU-2Q: sketch used for ADMISSION only (insert->main if sketch>=2 or ghost) on top of 2Q-CLOCK 18525923 (641); main back to freq-CLOCK. Finding so far: throughput tracks bytes/IO, not refaults (TinyLFU 600 had fewest refaults 16k); evicting fresh pages (scan-first, sampled LFU) seems to hurt

structural 2/3 (fix verifier: no pointer arithmetic on folio): hash-free CLOCK ref bits, slot = hash(i_ino, index) into 2^24-bit ARRAY bitmap; folio_accessed = loads + one store, no hash-map lookups, no list_move. v3 layout scan>256 / prob->gen if ref / gen CLOCK 2 passes

structural 2/3 (v7 = v6 SLRU+ghost + repeat-scan admission): scan-thread read of a page evicted within last 24k evictions (ghost window ~2x cache) goes to main instead of scan FIFO; scan re-reads of main pages refresh LRU but never promote to hot. Hypothesis: YCSB scan start keys are Zipfian so hot scan ranges repeat; every team policy discards them. v6=638, noop=634 on pc258; refaults flat ~16.5k across LRU/SLRU => GET retention not the lever.
tune 2Q-CLOCK 18525923 (641): probation share 1/4 -> 1/10 (S3-FIFO-like small queue), bigger freq-CLOCK main

structural 2/3 retry (fix verifier: zero-init tag vars). v7 = v6 SLRU+ghost + repeat-scan admission: scan-thread read of a page evicted within last 24k evictions goes to main instead of scan FIFO; scan re-reads of main pages refresh LRU, never promote to hot. Hypothesis: Zipfian scan start keys => repeating scan ranges, which all team policies discard. v6=638, noop=634 on pc258.
cross-host replication (reviewer): captain-ahab 2Q-CLOCK 18525923 (640.9 on ahab host) unchanged on my host pc318; my same-host v3 = 618.7

ARC-lite v1 (structural 1/3): scan FIFO (reserve 256) + prob (unread readahead) + once LRU + hot LRU (2nd read or ghost hit; cap 3/4 cache); ghost LRU_HASH 24k of evicted read pages. Evict scan>prob>once>hot. Hypothesis: tput ~ 1/misses-per-op, Zipf needs frequency
replication of 2Q-CLOCK 18525923 (641) unchanged, to check whether it is reliably >= noop (642) on pc257 or a lucky draw
composite on ahab 2Q-CLOCK (18525923; 621.1 on my host = my best): ghost LRU 16384 -> 65536 entries (~5x the ~12k-page cache) so long-distance refaults (19.7k/run) re-enter main directly

replication 2 of v6 SLRU+ghost array-metadata (ae41cad6, 638). Reviewer goal: per-host mean+-sd for top candidates vs noop. pc258 so far: noop 634; v3 649,627; v5 634; v6 638; v7 633. Conclusion so far: no policy distinguishable from noop; only large effect = scan-page hoarding (-20%).
replication of noop calibration 069942bd (642), comment-only change: 2Q-CLOCK replicated 641->612, so spread ~5%; need noop's spread to judge whether any team policy beats default reclaim

host calibration retry: unmodified noop (kernel default, never attaches) on my host pc318 — previous attempt 86392057 failed (dropped sys/stat.h). Tells whether ANY cache_ext policy beats kernel here (my best: 2Q-CLOCK 621.1/618.9, v3 618.7)

file-tail meta list on jack v3 (b65fa44f): last 8 pages of each file (LevelDB filter/index/footer) in own LRU capped 3072 pages, evicted after prob, before gen only when over cap. Tests whether table-open metadata reads are a big share of ios/op (team floor ~0.60-0.63 ios/op)

structural 3/3 (scan/2nd-level lane) v8 = v6 + exclusive caching: once-read pages go to HEAD of main (MRU-evicted) since LevelDB block cache holds that block right now; 2nd access -> hot (LRU). io_table skill: on pc258 every sane policy incl noop is pinned at ios/op~0.61, so only a lower ios/op can win; double-caching with block cache is the one untested source of waste.

2Q-CLOCK-ARRAY: identical decisions to 2Q-CLOCK 18525923 (641/612, mean 626) but per-folio meta + ghost moved from HASH/LRU_HASH maps to direct-mapped tagged ARRAYs (1M slots, 32K ghost). Tests the per-hook overhead lever (davy 9049727e: HASH meta cost ~3%); noop on pc257 = 642/639

ablation (reviewer): ahab 2Q-CLOCK (18525923; my host 621.1/618.9) WITHOUT the last-page-of-file eviction skip that every top policy carries. Hypothesis: pinning 1 page per SST forever can tie up a large share of the ~12k-page cache if the DB has thousands of SSTs. Context: on pc318 noop=631.4; ios/op of all decent policies incl noop is 0.60-0.62 (attempt-io-table)

2Q-CLOCK-ARRAY retry (rename struct slot -> ahab_slot, clashed with vmlinux.h): same decisions as 2Q-CLOCK 18525923 (mean 626) with direct-mapped tagged ARRAY meta+ghost instead of HASH maps; tests per-hook overhead lever

FALSIFICATION (reviewer, deliberately bad): v8 with eviction order inverted to hot > main > prob > scan. Question: does GET victim choice matter at all? LRU/SLRU/MRU-main (v3/v6/v8) all give ios/op 0.61 and refaults ~16.5-17k on pc258, same as noop. If this stays ~630, GET-side policy is irrelevant here; if it collapses, GET retention matters and all sane policies already saturate it.
replication run 2 of noop on pc318 (run 1 = 631.4, 5365201e). Building n>=2 same-host comparison noop vs best cache_ext (2Q-CLOCK 621.1/618.9, v3 618.7)

calibration run 2: unmodified noop on pc258 (comment-only). Reviewer conclusion so far: falsification 11a806f6 (GET hot/main evicted FIRST) cost only -4% for +27% refaults => throughput elasticity to refaults ~0.15; sane policies cut refaults ~15% vs noop => predicted +2%, matching observed v3/v6 mean ~637 vs noop 634. Need 2nd noop sample to judge.

structural 1/2 junk-first hybrid: we only evict probation (pages never re-accessed after insert: readahead neighbours/one-hit); 2nd access or ghost hit -> list_del + untrack so kernel LRU-2/workingset manages re-used pages; shortfall -> kernel reclaim. Noop (642/639) is best on pc257, so keep kernel for hot set and only remove junk
calibration: unmodified noop (kernel default; jack's 25d5e3f8 + trailing comment) on pc252 — my host lacks a noop reference; tells whether my 592-612 are host-level or policy-level

structural 1/3 Flag-2Q (overhead lane): NO folio_accessed hook, NO per-folio map. 2Q promotion test = kernel PG_active (set by folio_mark_accessed on 2nd access). prob_list (all new) -> PG_active promote to main FIFO, else evict; prob evicted while >1/4. Motivation: pc318 noop 631.4/628.1 beats best cache_ext (2Q-CLOCK 621.1/618.9, v3 618.7) by ~2% while ios/op is equal (0.61) => gap is per-hook overhead

replication of attached-empty floor aff0e4f2 (626): all 9 of my victim-proposing policies land 593-641 (wall ~40.8s) vs noop 642/639 and attached-empty (wall 42.4s). Tests whether attach is free and the cost lies in proposing victims

replication 3 of v6 SLRU+ghost array-metadata (ae41cad6: 638, 635). pc258 means so far: noop 632 (634,630); scan-first family ~635. Falsification 11a806f6: refault elasticity ~0.15 => policy ceiling over noop ~+2%.
replication 3 of v3 (b65fa44f: 649, 627). pc258 means: noop 632 (634,630); v6 632 (638,635,623). Testing whether v3 (no metadata, LRU main) differs from noop over 3 samples.

replication run 2 of jack v3 on pc318 (run 1 = 618.7, 264e80e8) for n=2 same-host comparison vs noop (631.4/628.1). Also: Flag-2Q 598.97 falsified 'accessed-hook overhead is the noop gap' (rios unchanged w/o accessed hook)

final: replication 3 of 2Q-CLOCK 18525923 (641, 612) for a 3-sample mean. Summary of my 20 evals on pc257: noop 642/639, attached-empty 626/635, every victim-proposing policy 593-641; scan-first eviction costs ~6% (593 vs 631 ablation c53d4286->bd194ffb); sampled-LFU eviction of fresh pages costs ~6%; HASH->ARRAY meta, TinyLFU admission, prob share no measurable effect

FINAL (20/20): v3 with SCAN_KEEP 256->32 (last untested scan-reserve point; 2048 was neutral). pc258 summary: v3 mean 638.3 (649,627,639) vs noop 632 (634,630) = +1%, best mean; v6 SLRU+ghost 632; falsification 11a806f6 shows refault elasticity ~0.15 so policy ceiling over noop is ~+2%.

workingset emulation v1 (structural 1/3, new lane): kernel-style inactive/active with two-touch activation (ref bit) + refault-DISTANCE-gated ghost (ts=evict_seq; activate on refault iff dist<=active size) + scan FIFO quarantine (256); active evicted only when > inactive; ARRAY tag state (jack v5 trick). Target: beat pc252 noop 633
replication run 3 of ahab 2Q-CLOCK (18525923) on pc318 (runs: 621.1, 618.9[ghost64k]). Same-host means so far: noop 629.8 (n=2), v3 612.3 (n=2), LFU+hist 579 (n=2)
replication run 3 of noop on pc318 (631.4, 628.1) to balance n=3 same-host comparison: 2Q-CLOCK 621.1/618.9/602.9, v3 618.7/605.9
reviewer replication on 3rd host: jack v3 SCAN_KEEP=32 (510f3bc0, 644 on pc258) unchanged on pc252; my noop here = 633. Tests 'v3 family beats noop' off its home host

fallback-share hybrid on jack v3 SCAN_KEEP=32 (510f3bc0; 611 on pc252, noop 633): every 4th evict_folios call returns nothing so kernel default reclaim runs (can reclaim non-watched pages). Tests the structural-handicap hypothesis: expect pgmajfault>22, resident->49MiB
fallback-share hybrid FALLBACK_EVERY=2 (half of evict_folios calls defer to kernel) on jack v3 keep32; FE=4 got 631.5, no-fallback 610.7, noop 633.2 on pc252. Dose-response test
noise replicate: noop on pc252 run 2 (run 1 = 633.2, 13c7f750). Gives pc252 its first identical-code pair for the team's noise estimate (Q3 in _open-questions)

FINAL 20/20 davy-jones: v3 run 3 on pc318. SYNTHESIS (same host pc318): noop 631.4/628.1/634.8 (mean 631.4) > 2Q-CLOCK 621.1/618.9/602.9 (614) ~ v3 618.7/605.9 (612) > CLOCK-bits 590 > S3-FIFO 585 > LFU+hist 572/587 > Flag-2Q 599. ios/op of all decent policies incl noop = 0.60-0.62 => hit-ratio lever ~exhausted (LevelDB block cache likely absorbs the hot head). Falsified: per-access hook cost explains the gap (Flag-2Q w/o accessed hook: rios unchanged); last-page pin is a cache drain (removal neutral, 615); bigger ghost helps (neutral). Hash-map overhead -3% (n=1, within noise).
replicate 2 of fallback-1/4 hybrid (961a0e71: 631.5) on pc252; noop here 633/641, v3-no-fallback 611, FE=2 600. Decides whether the hybrid recovers the BPF handicap
reviewer replication, 4th host: ahab 2Q-CLOCK (18525923, no scan special-casing; pc257 641/612/622, pc318 621/619/603) unchanged on pc252. noop here 633/641; scan-quarantine policies here 592-632

decomposition test: jack v3 keep32 with full hook list bookkeeping (add/move) but evict_folios proposes NOTHING (kernel does all reclaim). If ~noop (637 on pc252) the BPF handicap is in our eviction path/choices; if ~611 it is hook list-op cost

conservative-assist hybrid v1: track only scan-thread folios (ARRAY tag); propose victims from scan FIFO only when >1024 pages, else NOTHING (kernel decides). GET touch removes folio from our list. Motivation: eval-15 showed replacing kernel victims costs ~5%, hooks free. pc252 noop 633/641, no-victims 643

dose test: conservative-assist (scan-only victims >1024) rate-limited to 1 of 16 evict calls. Full-rate = 605.6, no-victims = 643.3, noop 633/641 on pc252. ~noop => cost scales with intervention volume; ~606 => any trickle of our victims flips kernel into a worse regime
dose test 2: conservative-assist scan-only victims (>1024) at 1 of 4 evict calls. Rate 0=643, 1/16=645, 1=606 on pc252 (noop 633/641). Looking for interior max above noop
replicate 2 of rate-1/16 scan-only-victim hybrid (624a8c66: 645.4) on pc252; noop 633/641. n=2 vs n=2 test of whether near-noop beats noop
final eval: noop run 3 on pc252 (runs 633.2, 641.3) to pin the noop mean against the near-noop hybrid (645.4, 643.7) and no-victims decomposition (643.3)
